Hi Claudia —

Thanks for the clear note and the SOW excerpt. Short answers up front: yes, we can accept a strong non-use (no-training/no-derivative) commitment for customer-provided prompts/responses, and we will impose the same contractual restrictions on our subprocessors. There are operational caveats I call out below.

Proposed DPA/SOW clause (draft language for legal):
"Redwood shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, responses, or derived outputs tied to Customer accounts) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models or models-as-a-service. Redwood represents and warrants that it will flow the same non-use obligations to any subprocessors and will not grant third parties rights to derive, resell, or otherwise exploit Customer Data for model training or derivative model development. Transformations performed by subprocessors for routing, anonymization, or format conversion shall be limited to operational purposes and shall not create downstream derivative ownership or rights."

Operational notes:
- Subprocessors: we will provide current subprocessor inventory and gate any new security-relevant subprocessors via 30-day notice + customer objection process for this account.
- Transformations: permitted transformations (e.g., tokenization, PII redaction, compression) are allowed strictly to enable routing and delivery; we will not claim any IP in transformed outputs.
- KMS/residency: onshore KMS is available as an enterprise option for Dedicated/Private customers. For Hosted customers we offer contractual controls and can add stricter contractual residency/KMS commitments for large governmental or regulated customers.

I attached a short redline with the proposed paragraph and two variants (one that explicitly mentions "no-derivative" and one that uses "no-training/no-improvement") — legal may prefer the latter for precision. cc'ing Kimberly to take a look and confirm the legal framing + whether we should accept their timing.

Attachments: redline_proposal_for_NMS.docx (docx)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that speeds things up.
